questions.question: The government of India to introduced a new economic policy in ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1991**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The government of India introduced a new economic policy in 1991, which marked a significant shift in India's economic structure.
 
• The policy is known for initiating economic liberalization, privatization, and globalization, often abbreviated as LPG.
 
• The reforms were aimed at opening up the Indian economy to the global market and reducing the control of the government on various economic activities.
 
• The 1991 economic policy was a response to a severe balance of payments crisis that India was facing at that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Liberalization**

 
 
• Economic liberalization refers to the process of reducing government regulations and restrictions in an economy to encourage greater participation of private entities.
 
• In the context of India, it involved reducing import tariffs, deregulating markets, and reducing taxes to attract foreign investment.
 
 
 
• **Privatization**
 
 
• Privatization is the transfer of ownership, property, or business from the government to the private sector.
 
• In India, this process involved the sale of state-owned enterprises to private entities to increase efficiency and profitability.
 
 
 
• **Globalization**
 
 
• Globalization is the process of interaction and integration among people, companies, and governments worldwide.
 
• In 1991, India embraced globalization by allowing foreign companies to operate in the Indian market and encouraging Indian companies to expand their operations globally.
 
 
 
• **Balance of Payments Crisis**
 
 
• The balance of payments crisis in India in 1991 was a situation where the country faced a severe shortage of foreign exchange reserves.
 
• To address this, India had to pledge its gold reserves to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and undertake significant economic reforms.

questions.question: What is the sex ratio in India as per the 2011 census (Females per Thousand Males)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**943**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The sex ratio in India as per the 2011 census is **943 females per 1000 males**.
 
• This figure represents an improvement from the 2001 census, where the sex ratio was 933 females per 1000 males.
 
• The sex ratio is an important indicator of gender balance in a population, reflecting the social and economic status of women in society.
 
• The 2011 census data was collected and compiled by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sex Ratio:**

 
 
• The sex ratio is defined as the number of females per 1000 males in a given population.
 
• It is a significant demographic indicator that helps in understanding the gender composition of a society.
 
• A balanced sex ratio is indicative of a healthy and equitable society where both genders have equal opportunities for survival and development.
 
• Historically, many regions have shown a skewed sex ratio due to cultural, social, and economic preferences for male children.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census:**
 
 
• The 2011 Census of India was the 15th National Census conducted since 1871.
 
• It was carried out in two phases: House listing and Housing Census (April to September 2010) and Population Enumeration (9th to 28th February 2011).
 
• The census provides comprehensive data on various demographic parameters including population size, sex ratio, literacy rate, and more.
 
• It serves as a critical tool for planning, policy formulation, and administration by the government.
 
 
 
• **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India:**
 
 
• The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India is responsible for conducting the decennial Census of India.
 
• This position is under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The organization collects, compiles, and publishes demographic data that is essential for national planning and development.

questions.question: Which dance form from West Bengal combines elements of classical dance with martial arts, and its movements often depict stories from Indian mythology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhau** is a traditional Indian dance form that combines elements of classical dance with martial arts.
 
• It is particularly popular in the states of **West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand**.
 
• The movements in Chhau often depict stories from Indian mythology, including the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas.
 
• **Masks** are a significant aspect of the dance, especially in the Purulia Chhau from West Bengal, where dancers wear elaborate and colorful masks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is one of the eight major Indian classical dances.
 
• It originated in a village named Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance form is known for its impressive footwork and expressive eye movements.
 
• It typically narrates stories from Hindu epics and Puranas.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by intricate body movements and expressive gestures.
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest surviving dance forms in India, with roots tracing back to ancient temples.
 
• The dance often depicts religious themes and spiritual ideas.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam**
 
 
• Mohiniattam is a classical dance form from Kerala.
 
• It is known for its graceful movements and feminine style.
 
• The term "Mohiniattam" comes from "Mohini" (a mythical enchantress) and "attam" (graceful body movements).
 
• This dance form primarily focuses on themes of love and devotion.
 
 
 
• **Chhau**
 
 
• Chhau is performed during festivals and special occasions.
 
• There are three main styles of Chhau: Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).
 
• Purulia Chhau uses masks, while the other two styles do not.
 
• The dance involves vigorous and energetic movements, often resembling martial arts.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the first woman Chairperson of the Railway Board?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaya Varma Sinha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jaya Varma Sinha has become the **first woman to be appointed as the Chairperson of the Railway Board**, the apex body of the Indian Railways.
 
• Her appointment marks a significant milestone in the history of Indian Railways, reflecting the growing role of women in leadership positions within the organization.
 
• Before being appointed as the Chairperson, **she has held various key positions within the Indian Railways**, showcasing her extensive experience and expertise in the field.
 
• Jaya Varma Sinha is known for her **dedication and contributions to the development and modernization of the Indian Railways**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Railway Board**

 
 
• The Railway Board is the apex body of the Indian Railways and functions under the Ministry of Railways, Government of India.
 
• It is responsible for the overall administration, management, and policy formulation for the Indian Railways.
 
• The Railway Board consists of a Chairman, a Financial Commissioner, and other functional members who oversee various aspects such as engineering, traffic, mechanical, and staff services.
 
• The Board plays a crucial role in the planning and execution of railway projects, ensuring the efficient functioning of the vast railway network in India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railways**
 
 
• Indian Railways is one of the largest railway networks in the world, operating under the Ministry of Railways, Government of India.
 
• It plays a vital role in the transportation of passengers and goods across the country, connecting remote areas and facilitating economic growth.
 
• Indian Railways has a vast network of tracks, trains, stations, and employees, making it a critical component of India's infrastructure.
 
• The organization is constantly working on modernization and expansion projects to improve efficiency, safety, and passenger experience.
 
 
 
• **Women in Leadership**
 
 
• The appointment of women in leadership roles is a significant step towards gender equality and empowerment.
 
• It reflects the growing recognition of women's capabilities and contributions in various fields, including traditionally male-dominated sectors like railways.
 
• Encouraging women to take up leadership positions helps in fostering diversity and bringing diverse perspectives to decision-making processes.
 
• Organizations benefit from inclusive leadership, which can lead to better problem-solving, innovation, and overall performance.

questions.question: In India, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed ___________ of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-third**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State in India shall not exceed **one-third** of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State.
 
• However, the total number of members in the Legislative Council should not be less than 40.
 
• The provision for the Legislative Council is given in Article 171 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Not all states in India have a Legislative Council; it exists only in a few states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative Council**

 
 
• Also known as Vidhan Parishad, it is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• Members of the Legislative Council are either elected by the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, or are nominated by the Governor.
 
• The tenure of a member of the Legislative Council is 6 years, with one-third of the members retiring every 2 years.
 
• The presence of a Legislative Council helps in providing a revising chamber to the Legislative Assembly and acts as a check on hasty legislation.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Assembly**
 
 
• Also known as Vidhan Sabha, it is the lower house of the state legislature in India.
 
• Members of the Legislative Assembly are directly elected by the people of the state through general elections.
 
• The tenure of the Legislative Assembly is 5 years unless dissolved sooner.
 
• The Legislative Assembly is responsible for making laws on the state list and concurrent list subjects, as well as controlling the state's finances.

questions.question: Who has won the prestigious ‘Eni Award,’ which is considered among the top global honours for scientific research in energy and environment in July 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thalappil Pradeep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thalappil Pradeep is a renowned Indian scientist known for his groundbreaking work in the field of nanotechnology and materials science.
 
• He has made significant contributions to the development of affordable clean water technologies, which have been recognized globally.
 
• The Eni Award is one of the most prestigious international awards for scientific research in energy and the environment, highlighting Pradeep's exceptional achievements.
 
• His innovative work includes the creation of nanomaterials that can remove contaminants from water, providing clean drinking water solutions to millions of people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eni Award**

 
 
• The Eni Award is an annual international award established by the Italian energy company Eni in 2007.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Nobel Prize for Energy" and aims to promote better use of energy sources and increased environmental research.
 
• The award recognizes outstanding research and technological innovation in the fields of energy efficiency, renewable energy, and environmental protection.
 
• Winners receive a gold medal specially minted by the Italian State Mint and a cash prize.
 
 
 
• **Nanotechnology**
 
 
• Nanotechnology involves the manipulation of matter on an atomic, molecular, and supramolecular scale.
 
• Applications of nanotechnology are vast and include medicine, electronics, biomaterials, and energy production.
 
• Thalappil Pradeep's work primarily focuses on using nanotechnology to develop sustainable and cost-effective solutions for water purification.
 
 
 
• **Water Purification Technologies**
 
 
• Water purification technologies are essential for providing clean drinking water and ensuring public health.
 
• These technologies include physical processes such as filtration, sedimentation, and distillation, as well as chemical processes like chlorination and the use of advanced materials.
 
• Thalappil Pradeep has developed novel nanomaterials that can effectively remove contaminants such as heavy metals and pathogens from water, making it safe for consumption.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the founding father of modern economics?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Adam Smith**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ • Adam Smith is often referred to as the "Father of Modern Economics". • He wrote the seminal work "An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations" in 1776. • Smith's theories laid the foundation for classical economics and the concept of the free market. • He introduced the idea of the "invisible hand", which suggests that the self-regulating nature of the market leads to economic prosperity.

questions.question: __________ represents a potential for further intellectual growth and contribution to economic-socio-cultural development of society.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Literacy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Literacy enables individuals to acquire knowledge and develop critical thinking skills, which are essential for personal and societal growth.
 
• High literacy rates are often correlated with economic development and social progress, as literate populations are better equipped to participate in the economy and contribute to social and cultural advancements.
 
• Literacy is a fundamental human right and a cornerstone for achieving other rights, empowering individuals to improve their living standards and participate fully in community and national affairs.
 
• Promoting literacy can help reduce poverty and inequality by providing people with the skills needed to access better employment opportunities and improve their quality of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census**

 
 
• A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• It is conducted periodically by governments to collect data on the population's size, distribution, and various demographic characteristics.
 
• This data is crucial for planning and delivering public services, such as healthcare, education, and infrastructure.
 
• In many countries, censuses are conducted every ten years.
 
 
 
• **Economy**
 
 
• The economy refers to the system of production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services within a society or geographic area.
 
• It encompasses various sectors, including agriculture, industry, and services, and is influenced by factors such as government policies, market conditions, and global trends.
 
• Economic growth is often measured by indicators such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and employment rates.
 
• Economic stability and growth are essential for improving living standards and reducing poverty.
 
 
 
• **Politics**
 
 
• Politics involves the activities associated with governance, including the formulation and implementation of policies, laws, and regulations.
 
• It encompasses various institutions and processes, such as elections, political parties, and government agencies.
 
• Political systems can vary widely, from democracies to authoritarian regimes, each with different approaches to governance and citizen participation.
 
• Effective political governance is crucial for maintaining social order, protecting citizens' rights, and promoting economic and social development.

questions.question: The portion of agricultural produce which is sold in the market by the farmers is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**marketed surplus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Marketed surplus** refers to the portion of agricultural produce that is sold in the market by farmers after meeting their own consumption and other non-commercial needs.
 
• This surplus is a critical indicator of the level of commercialization in agriculture, reflecting how much of the produce is available for trade and sale.
 
• The marketed surplus can vary widely depending on the type of crop, the level of agricultural productivity, and the economic conditions of the farmers.
 
• A higher marketed surplus generally indicates better economic conditions for farmers and a more vibrant agricultural market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Produce**

 
 
• Agricultural produce includes all the crops, fruits, vegetables, and other products that are cultivated or grown by farmers.
 
• These products can be for personal consumption, feeding livestock, or for selling in the market.
 
 
 
• **Produced Surplus**
 
 
• Produced surplus refers to the total agricultural output that exceeds the needs of the farmer's household and is available for sale or trade.
 
• It is a broader term that includes marketed surplus but also considers any surplus that may not be immediately sold in the market.
 
 
 
• **Marketed Deficit**
 
 
• Marketed deficit refers to a situation where the agricultural produce is insufficient to meet the market demand.
 
• This can lead to higher prices and potential food shortages.
 
 
 
• **Produced Deficit**
 
 
• Produced deficit occurs when the total agricultural production is less than what is needed for both consumption and market sale.
 
• This could be due to poor yield, adverse weather conditions, or other factors affecting agricultural productivity.

questions.question: __________ is swim on the back in swimming.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Backstroke**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Backstroke** is one of the four main swimming styles used in competitive swimming.
 
• It involves swimmers lying on their backs and using an alternating arm stroke and a flutter kick.
 
• The backstroke is unique because it is the only stroke that is swum on the back, providing a different breathing pattern compared to other strokes.
 
• It is also known for being a relatively fast stroke, second only to the freestyle in terms of speed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Streamline**

 
 
• Streamline is a technique used in swimming to reduce drag and improve speed.
 
• It involves the swimmer positioning their body in a straight line, with arms extended above the head, hands together, and body tight.
 
• This position is often used at the start of a race or after a turn to maximize speed before beginning the stroke.
 
 
 
• **Butterfly Stroke**
 
 
• The butterfly stroke is another competitive swimming stroke, known for its demanding technique and high energy consumption.
 
• It involves a simultaneous arm movement and a dolphin kick, where both legs move together in a wave-like motion.
 
• This stroke is considered one of the most challenging due to the coordination and strength required.
 
 
 
• **Freestyle**
 
 
• Freestyle is the fastest and most popular swimming stroke in competitive swimming.
 
• Swimmers use an alternating arm stroke and a flutter kick, similar to the backstroke but performed on the stomach.
 
• There are no specific rules on how to swim freestyle, which allows swimmers to use any technique they find fastest, although the front crawl is most commonly used.

questions.question: T. Balasaraswati is related to which of the following dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• T. Balasaraswati was one of the most renowned exponents of **Bharatnatyam**, a classical dance form from Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• She was instrumental in popularizing Bharatnatyam globally and was known for her expressive abhinaya (the art of expression in Indian classical dance).
 
• T. Balasaraswati received several prestigious awards, including the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, for her contributions to the art form.
 
• Her performances were highly acclaimed for their depth, emotional intensity, and technical precision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatnatyam:**

 
 
• Bharatnatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• The dance form is traditionally performed by women and has its roots in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It comprises three main elements: Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressive dance), and Natya (dramatic dance).
 
 
 
• **Kathak:**
 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form from Northern India, characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive storytelling.
 
• The word 'Kathak' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Katha,' meaning story, and the dance form traditionally involves the narration of stories from epics and mythology.
 
 
 
• **Odissi:**
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form from Odisha, known for its fluid movements, sculpturesque poses, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• It has a strong connection with the temples of Odisha and often depicts stories of Lord Jagannath.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali:**
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama from Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes, detailed makeup, and face masks.
 
• It combines dance, drama, and music to depict tales from Hindu epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana.

questions.question: The lastand __________ tirthankara of the Jainas was Vardhamana Mahavira.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vardhamana Mahavira is the 24th and last Tirthankara in Jainism.
 
• He was born in 540 BC in a royal family in present-day Bihar, India.
 
• Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana (omniscience) after 12 years of rigorous penance.
 
• He propagated the principles of Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy), and Aparigraha (non-attachment).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tirthankara**

 
 
• In Jainism, a Tirthankara is a savior and spiritual teacher of the dharma (righteous path).
 
• The word 'Tirthankara' signifies the creator of a Tirtha (a fordable passage across the sea of interminable births and deaths).
 
• There are 24 Tirthankaras in Jainism, with Rishabhanatha being the first and Mahavira being the last.
 
 
 
• **Ahimsa (Non-Violence)**
 
 
• Ahimsa is a fundamental principle in Jainism advocating non-violence and respect for all living beings.
 
• It is considered the highest ethical value and a way of life in Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Kevala Jnana**
 
 
• Kevala Jnana means absolute knowledge or omniscience.
 
• It is the highest form of knowledge and is attained through rigorous penance and purification of the soul.
 
 
 
• **Five Great Vows**
 
 
• The five great vows (Mahavratas) are Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy), and Aparigraha (non-attachment).
 
• These vows are the ethical foundation of Jain monastic life and a guideline for lay followers.

questions.question: Which maestro of the tabla, a percussion instrument, is regarded as one of the greatest musicians in the world and has collaborated with numerous international artists?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zakir Hussain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Zakir Hussain** is widely regarded as one of the greatest tabla players in the world.
 
• He is known for his collaborations with numerous international artists and has brought the tabla to the global stage.
 
• He was born on March 9, 1951, and is the son of legendary tabla player Alla Rakha.
 
• Tabla maestro **Ustad Zakir Hussain** received the following prestigious awards from the Government of India:
 
 
• **Padma Shri** – **1988**
 
• **Padma Bhushan** – **2002**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla**

 
 
• The tabla is a pair of twin hand drums from the Indian subcontinent, used in traditional, classical, popular, and folk music.
 
• The right-hand drum is called the "dayan" and is smaller in size and higher in pitch, while the left-hand drum is called the "bayan" and is larger and lower in pitch.
 
• Tabla playing involves intricate finger and hand movements to produce a variety of sounds and rhythms.
 
 
 
• **Collaborations**
 
 
• Zakir Hussain has worked with a plethora of international artists, including George Harrison, John McLaughlin, and Yo-Yo Ma.
 
• He has been a part of fusion bands like Shakti, which blends Indian classical music with jazz.
 
 
 
• **Musical Legacy**
 
 
• Zakir Hussain continues to inspire new generations of musicians and tabla players around the world.
 
• He has also composed music for films and has been involved in various educational initiatives to promote Indian classical music.

questions.question: Philosophers classified matter in the form of how many basic elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Philosophers in ancient times often categorized matter into five basic elements, which are Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Ether (or Space).
 
• These classifications were foundational in various ancient philosophies and are still referenced in modern discussions of classical elements.
 
• This concept is found in various cultures, including ancient Greek philosophy (Empedocles), Hinduism, Buddhism, and traditional Chinese philosophy.
 
• The idea was that all physical matter in the universe was composed of these five elements in different proportions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earth (Prithvi)**

 
 
• Represents solidity and stability.
 
• Associated with qualities like heaviness, fixity, and a downward motion.
 
• In the human body, it is related to bones, muscles, and tissues.
 
 
 
• **Water (Ap or Jala)**
 
 
• Represents fluidity and cohesion.
 
• Associated with qualities like coolness, liquidity, and a downward and outward motion.
 
• In the human body, it is related to blood, lymph, and other bodily fluids.
 
 
 
• **Fire (Agni or Tejas)**
 
 
• Represents transformation and energy.
 
• Associated with qualities like heat, light, and upward motion.
 
• In the human body, it is related to metabolism and digestion.
 
 
 
• **Air (Vayu)**
 
 
• Represents movement and expansion.
 
• Associated with qualities like lightness, dryness, and an upward and outward motion.
 
• In the human body, it is related to breath and the movement of muscles and nerves.
 
 
 
• **Ether (Akasha)**
 
 
• Represents space and subtlety.
 
• Associated with qualities like lightness, clarity, and non-resistance.
 
• In the human body, it is related to cavities and spaces like the mouth, nostrils, and thoracic cavity.

questions.question: The Dandi March, led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, was a significant protest against which British policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt tax**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Dandi March, also known as the Salt March, was a non-violent protest against the British monopoly on salt and the heavy salt tax imposed on Indians.
 
• Beginning on **March 12, 1930**, Gandhi and his followers marched from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi in Gujarat, covering approximately 240 miles over 24 days. 
 
• Upon reaching Dandi on **April 6, 1930**, Gandhi symbolically made salt from seawater, defying British law and sparking a widespread civil disobedience movement across India.
 
• The protest against the salt tax highlighted the unjust and oppressive policies of British rule and became a turning point in the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indigo Cultivation
 
 
• Indigo cultivation was forced upon Indian farmers under British rule, especially in Bengal and Bihar, to meet the high demand for indigo dye in Europe.
 
• The exploitative system led to the Indigo Rebellion (1859–1860) and later influenced movements like the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917, where Gandhi supported farmers against the oppressive indigo cultivation practices enforced by British planters.
 
 
 
• Textile Trade Regulations
 
 
• The British imposed trade regulations and heavy duties on Indian textiles while promoting British-made textiles in India.
 
• This led to the decline of India’s traditional textile industry, particularly handloom and Khadi.
 
• In response, the Swadeshi Movement (1905) encouraged Indians to boycott British goods, especially textiles, and promoted the use of Indian-made products, including Khadi, to revive the local industry.
 
 
 
• Land Revenue
 
 
• The British introduced various exploitative land revenue systems like the Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari systems, which led to excessive taxation and poverty among Indian farmers.
 
• Resistance to these policies included the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and other regional revolts where farmers protested against unfair land taxes and evictions.

questions.question: Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution mention provisions related to which of the following rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Right to Equality**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution mention provisions related to Right to Equality.
 
• **Article 14**: Guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within India.
 
• **Article 15**: Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• **Article 16**: Ensures equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• **Article 17**: Abolishes "untouchability" and prohibits its practice in any form.
 
• **Article 18**: Abolishes titles (except for military or academic distinctions) to promote social equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28)
 
 
• Article 25: Ensures the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• Article 26: Allows every religious denomination or section to manage its own affairs in matters of religion.
 
• Article 27: Prohibits the state from compelling any person to pay taxes for the promotion of any particular religion.
 
• Article 28: Prohibits religious instruction in educational institutions wholly funded by the state.
 
 
 
• Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24)
 
 
• Article 23: Prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and similar forms of exploitation.
 
• Article 24: Prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 in hazardous occupations.
 
 
 
• Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22)
 
 
• Article 19: Provides six freedoms, including freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• Article 20: Protects against arbitrary conviction by providing safeguards against double jeopardy, self-incrimination, and ex post facto laws.
 
• Article 21: Guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty, a core fundamental right.
 
• Article 22: Provides protections against arrest and detention in certain cases, including rights to be informed of grounds of arrest and to consult a lawyer.

questions.question: Which of the following is the last five year plan of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __the__ __**Twelfth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–2017) was the last officially implemented Five-Year Plan in India.
 
• After this, the planning process was discontinued, and the NITI Aayog was established in 2015 to replace the Planning Commission,
 
 
• shifting focus to a long-term development strategy rather than fixed-term plans.
 
 
 
• The Twelfth Plan aimed to promote inclusive growth, ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reached all sections of society, especially marginalized groups.
 
• The plan emphasized sustainable development, focusing on environmental sustainability and reducing the carbon footprint of economic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India), which shifted the focus from fixed-term planning to a more flexible approach to policy-making and governance.
 
• The NITI Aayog emphasizes long-term vision and strategy, moving away from the traditional Five-Year Plans.
 
• Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997–2002)
 
 
• The Ninth Plan prioritized human development, aiming to improve the quality of life through initiatives in health, education, and employment.
 
• It recognized the importance of investing in human capital to drive economic growth.
 
• A key objective was to reduce poverty and enhance social justice.
 
• The plan introduced various poverty alleviation programs and targeted interventions to uplift marginalized sections of society, with a goal to reduce the poverty ratio significantly.
 
 
 
• Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007)
 
 
• The Tenth Plan aimed for a GDP growth rate of 8% per annum, emphasizing job creation and improving the employment situation in India. It recognized the need for inclusive growth to ensure that the benefits of economic development reached all sectors of society.
 
• This plan also focused on enhancing infrastructure, particularly in rural areas, to facilitate economic activities. Investments were directed towards transportation, power, and irrigation, crucial for agricultural productivity and overall economic growth.
 
 
 
• Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–2012)
 
 
• The Eleventh Plan aimed for a GDP growth rate of 9% per annum, focusing on creating jobs and reducing poverty.
 
• It sought to build a competitive and sustainable economy by promoting innovation and entrepreneurship.
 
• It emphasized social inclusion, targeting the needs of disadvantaged groups.
 
• The plan aimed to enhance access to quality education, health services, and basic amenities, ensuring that development was equitable and inclusive.
